questions.question_text: Four batteries are taken from a drawer and tested. Which event is the complement of 'at least one battery is flat'?

options.why: Exactly one is only one of the ways of getting at least one flat battery.
This can happen at the same time as at least one being flat, so it is not the complement.
Names the strongest form of the event rather than the outcomes it leaves out.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of 'at least one' is 'none'.
The complementary event is 'no battery is flat'.

options.why: Repeated the given probability instead of subtracting it from $1$.
Doubled the given probability because there are two clocks, instead of subtracting from $1$.
Squared the given probability instead of subtracting it from $1$.

questions.question_text: A netballer scores from any shot with probability $\frac{1}{4}$, and her shots are independent. She takes three shots. What is the probability that she scores at least one goal?

options.why: Found the probability of scoring no goals but did not subtract it from $1$.
Found the probability of scoring from all three shots instead of at least one.
Multiplied $\frac{1}{4}$ by $3$, treating 'at least one' as three separate chances.
Found the probability that neither battery is flat but did not subtract it from $1$.
Left the total at $9$ for the second draw instead of reducing it to $8$.
Found the probability that both batteries are flat instead of at least one.

questions.question_text: A string of fairy lights lights up only when all four of its globes work. The probability that all four globes work is $0.88$. What is the probability that at least one globe does not work?

options.why: Repeated the probability that all four globes work instead of subtracting it from $1$.
Divided $0.88$ by $4$ to get 'one globe' rather than using the complement.
Divided the complement by $4$, as if the chance were shared equally between the globes.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of 'at least one does not work' is 'all four work'.
$P(\text{at least one does not work}) = 1 - 0.88$
$= 0.12$

Subtracts the probability that both clocks ring rather than the probability that neither rings.
Adds the two ringing probabilities, giving a value greater than $1$.

questions.solution_text:
The complement of 'at least one rings' is 'neither rings'.
$P(\text{neither rings}) = 0.1 \times 0.1$
$= 0.01$
$P(\text{at least one rings}) = 1 - 0.01$
$= 0.99$

questions.question_text: A netballer scores from any shot with probability $\frac{1}{3}$, and her shots are independent. She takes three shots. What is the probability that she scores at least two goals?

options.why: Found the probability of scoring fewer than two goals but did not subtract it from $1$.
Found the probability of at least one goal by subtracting only the no-goals path.
Found the probability of scoring from all three shots instead of at least two.

questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{no goals}) = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3}$
$= \frac{8}{27}$
$P(\text{goal, miss, miss}) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3}$
$= \frac{4}{27}$
The single goal could be the first, second or third shot.
$P(\text{exactly one goal}) = 3 \times \frac{4}{27}$
$= \frac{12}{27}$
$P(\text{fewer than two goals}) = \frac{8}{27} + \frac{12}{27}$
$= \frac{20}{27}$
$P(\text{at least two goals}) = 1 - \frac{20}{27}$
$= \frac{7}{27}$

questions.question_text: A box contains $11$ light globes, $4$ of which are faulty. Three globes are taken out one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that at least one globe is faulty?

options.why: Found the probability that no globe is faulty but did not subtract it from $1$.
Gave the probability that the first globe taken is faulty instead of using all three draws.
Found the probability that all three globes are faulty instead of at least one.
